summary:
Turn 64 reviewed the re-executed C1 check against the amended claim, which restores the agreement finding's basis.

State on entry. The F2 scope clarification had bumped C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector to version 2 and left every C1 artifact with the blocker "Direct-check semantic inputs changed; execution requires rechecking", so the C1 conclusion was an investigation lead. The re-submitted check executed as artifact a0f10ee024ac4ba38d3b84b21a8b40f3 (run 32aff0d098454dc78bec6a3916753fa9) with outcome violated and the oracle correspondence unreviewed; its stream shows the same canonical sequence as the reviewed three-property artifact (recovery_seed, peer_committed_reply, recovery_resolution, accept_round_after_commit, recovery_outcome, commit_propagation_divergence).

Review judgement (checker_correspondence, no_issue_found). Increment and unchanged parts: the F2 amended only the claim's scope text — it now states that the obligation ends at adopting the reported committed vector and names claim C3 for applied-state agreement — while the check's entry, prefix, schedule, prerequisites, identity fields, predicates and harness bytes are the reviewed ones, so the fresh execution asks the same question of the same code. What it observed: the resolution still does not adopt a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED (adopted_committed false), the recoverer and the committed peer still differ (vectors_match false), and the disagreement still survives the Commit broadcast (all_committed_match false with NOOP against PUT and NOOP). Correspondence: the three monitored properties encode the obligation as amended; the committed-reply prerequisite is admitted with instance identity correlation; the harness drives the queued rounds and re-reads InstanceSpace after each delivery; and the prepared committed record plus substituted trigger remain the declared applicability. Alternatives and limits: the applied-state property is deliberately absent here and belongs to C3, exactly as the amended scope states; the pre-amendment artifacts keep their observations but stay superseded for basis; and the original applicability limits (prepared record, direct entry, N=3 Thrifty) are unchanged.

Effect. Once accepted, the C1 agreement finding is confirmed again on the current wording, alongside the untouched promoted-leader variant C6 and the other eight settled claims. The lesson from last turn stands: amending a claim's scope text forces re-execution of its artifacts, so such clarifications should be batched or avoided late in a run.
